Hey i want to improve the apparatus's ability to give feedback on what is happening during a search in the first place, a few things that are off to me about the You know, there's just a few things that are kind of off to me about the current experience. When I head to Twine, dialogue, and I go to the editor, I head to, you know, the side panel, the editorial board. I go to the apparatus, and there's just a few things that I kind of have problems with. One, I think, like, it's difficult to understand exactly when the agents are running and what they're exactly doing. I'd like to have, like, a really detailed look at exactly what sources the agents are looking for and whether they're doing that, and to restart if there's, like, some sort of failure. I need, like, more failure bounce, like to make sure that things are errors are actually being caught, that the right details are actually being looked at, possibly even having an ability to steer the agent search. That would be, like, if you're opening the full apparatus, I think being able to steer the search is probably important. Like, hey, like there's some steering involved here. I think that would be an excellent addition. Right now, when I go and I try out the apparatus, there's, like, a huge issue, at least to me, where there's no steering involved. That sounds, like that can sound kind of nice, but when an option isn't there, like let's say I highlight things in my text, right? I highlight stuff. That gives me some options, of course, in my compositor. But if I want to say, like, just have this immediately do, like a search to get information on this particular thing, you know? Like, oh sure, I can go and, like there should be some sort of right-click. Like sure, I can search Google for stuff if I right-click, or I can ask Gemini or something. But I want something better. I want something more involved, more important for the right-click on this site, or for, like, a hover option so that I can get, hey, immediately, hey, you know, in the regular editor, I can have, you know, go get sources. You know, there should be a get sources option or something like that. And it's like, yeah, this is the thing that you need to go and do some research on now. Like if I want to provide more information on this particular thing, like go and find sources on this, go and find the original source, that sort of stuff. That should all be there in the apparatus. Like the apparatus feature is, it feels more tacked on than what I think it really could provide. The other thing is, like, there's options. If we look at the marginalia, it's just, it just, there's some parts of it which I feel, it just feels a little bit, how do I say this? Feels a little tacked on, right? Like if you look at it, it just seems like it's tacked on. I personally, I feel like the marginalia should be taken out of the editorial board, and it should be, like, some option, like on the side here should be, like a prompt here. Maybe even thinking of a total alternative to the editorial board, where we pull the editorial board outside, outside of the side weird side panel, and we have it in the center of the screen, at, like, at the, like, bottom of the screen, right? Like where you can immediately start prompting, start talking, like go and see, and the overlay where you have, like, on the side, the comments, like, and not like a side panel, but, like, if you look at the Google Docs experience. The Google Docs experience has, like, these comments on the side. It has, like, oh, this is where this comment is looking at, this is what this is looking at. It's a more involved experience, and it's just all right there. Like users can hop in and dive in immediately with the text, and that makes it so that they never really need to pull out of the text, and I kind of like that as a design idea. So let's go with that. I like this pathway forward in order to improve, like, our ability to do design. If we think about the cards, the different cards that we can have, the way that we can mesh in with the styling, like remember we're very, like typewriter-esque styling. So working with that and even adding, like, yeah, so, like, that's important. I like everything else so far. Like it's just a generally good idea. If we go to, like, a new folio or whatever, that all works. I like everything else. Yeah, let's just get that part finished and done with.
